best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers an unconditional 10% Energy Regen% and 80% Coordinated DMG boost. Also grants a passive supportive effect upon a Coordinated Attack CRIT, giving 20% ATK to the on-field active character. Offers a nice blend of personal damage and buffing.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers 12% Electro DMG and 12% Resonance Skill DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, awkward to use due to the long Transform animation.

best_echo_sets.commentary: This set sacrifices Yinlin's personal damage in order to provide higher buffing to a single character. It provides an extra 10% Energy Regen to the wielder unconditionally and gives 22.5% ATK to the incoming character for 15s after casting Outro skill.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: The best and only real option 5P Moonlit Clouds has, as it grants an extra 12% DMG Bonus on top of the ATK boost to the next character that Moonlit Clouds would usually give. Additionally restores a lot of Energy to the caster when it deals damage.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Yinlin's signature Rectifier is easily one of the best generalist options in the game and her best in slot. It gives massive ATK, CRIT Rate and DMG Bonus buffs, with an ATK% buff that's only further increased in quickswap which makes it stand even higher above the options below.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Yinlin is a 5-star Electro Rectifier Hybrid character capable of Coordinated Attacks, Electro and Liberation DMG buffing, decently fast rotations, and relatively good personal damage, who also is quite good in Quickswap teams. Yet, she is characterized by her crucial lack of notoriety in the meta. What does she actually do, and why is she so notoriously replaceable? Let's explore that more in-depth.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: The focal point of Yinlin's kit is her Forte Circuit. Her Forte gauge stacks up to 100 points, and it's regenerated through her Basic Attacks and Skill. Once it's full, she can cast a Forte Heavy Attack which enables her to trigger Coordinated Attacks. How she does this is through marking enemies. She does so through 3 different stages.

The first of these is Sinner's Mark. It's applied on enemies hit by her Intro, Ultimate and Basic Attacks. It can then be upgraded through her Skill, which allows Yinlin to trigger up to 4 Electromagnetic Blasts on enemies hit by her on-field Basic Attacks. Finally, it can be converted into Punishment Mark by her Forte Heavy Attack. As we explained earlier, this enables her to trigger a Coordinated Attack on enemies hit once per second, for a duration of 18s.

One thing worth noting about her Electromagnetic Blasts is that they will individually count towards her Forte and Concerto generation in AoE situations, per enemy hit by them. In other words, in AoE scenarios, Yinlin can charge up her Forte and Concerto gauges much quicker than normal, which can allow her to speed up her rotations drastically.

The key idea when it comes to Yinlin's rotation is to apply her Sinner's Mark and upgrade it through her Skill very quickly, to start generating some Forte and Concerto through a mix of her Skills and Basic or Heavy Attacks. Yinlin has 2 Skills that can be chained consecutively and each generate a great amount of Forte and Concerto, her Ultimate is a nice burst of damage and Concerto as well, and finally her Forte Heavy can finish the rotation as the last big burst of Concerto that she gets.

When it comes to buffs, Yinlin is very simple: the only buff that she can provide is a 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplification for 14s, expiring on swap, through her Outro. Her passives do give her a free 15% CRIT Rate and up to 20% ATK for her on-field rotation, but that doesn't really change much beyond slightly raising her personal damage potential.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: As we're sure you could guess from the above explanation, Yinlin's only buff being her Outro Skill really doesn't make her anything special in the Wuthering Waves meta. Every limited Hybrid buffer that followed her had some sort of special buff to give on top of this, like Zhezhi's Energy generation or Roccia's team-wide flat ATK buff. Yinlin only has 2 things to contribute to the team, her Outro and personal damage. That's it.

While Yinlin has a great uptime on her Coordinated Attacks and they deal a lot of personal damage, her rotation is fast, and she gained access to the Empyrean Anthem Echo set which raised her ceiling a bit since her release, she really has nothing too useful to provide to the team due to a crucial lack of unique buffing capabilities. Zhezhi immediately powercrept her in the Jinhsi team very shortly after Jinhsi's own release, and Xiangli Yao and Calcharo were never good to begin with. In other words: Ever since her release, Yinlin did nothing special, and was nothing special.

While she has Quickswap potential, and she has personal damage, Changli is simply an upgraded Yinlin in this role, and Lynae has completely powercrept Yinlin in any team she could ever exist in, Quickswap or not. She has way, way more buffs, a modern and cohesive kit, and her similar personal damage and rotation time make Lynae so much more useful than Yinlin in all Liberation DMG teams, including Electro ones, it's not even comparable. As a final nail in the coffin, practically no Electro damage dealers have been released since Xiangli Yao, and when they did, F2P options wound up better than Yinlin. Take Augusta with Mortefi, or Hsin with Electro Rover, or Suoming with Sanhua as examples. Electro/Liberation is a combination of damage types Yinlin needs to be present on a character for her to be justified on any team, and no damage dealer has released with those damage types since Xiangli Yao, where Lynae powercrept Yinlin, and where Changli has always been better in Quickswap.

In conclusion, Yinlin is one of the worst limited characters in Wuthering Waves. From a meta standpoint, we advise skipping this character. Unless you really, really are fond of Yinlin, generally speaking, the investment is not worth it. She retains some okay-ish usability in a select few teams if you already own her though, so she isn't completely unusable if she is present on your account. Still, her weapon Stringmaster is a great generalist Rectifier DPS choice and is much, much higher priority than Yinlin herself considering her current meta situation (even still, we currently recommend pulling Signature Rectifiers for the DPS you choose to pull rather than Stringmaster).

synergies.commentary: Yinlin's best synergy nowadays is with Main DPS Iuno, as Iuno has one of the highest Liberation DMG potentials in the game and Yinlin is only outclassed by a Ciaccona with her Signature weapon equipped. Yinlin provides good on and off-field damage as well as 25% Liberation DMG Amplify to Iuno which makes her a close second best choice to Ciaccona.

Yinlin's Coordinated Attacks, personal damage, small buffs she provides to Jinhsi's Ultimate via Outro and general buffs with Echoes, and her swap cancel windows at a less casual level, make Jinhsi and Yinlin a competitive pair to Zhezhi (while being a bit worse), and one of the best teams in the game.

Due to Yinlin's good personal off-field damage, but most importantly her extremely important 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplify on Outro, she can buff Xiangli Yao by ludicrous amounts and make him a top DPS.

Yinlin should only be considered in Augusta teams as a worse option than Mortefi. This is because while she has slightly higher personal damage, it doesn't compensate for her smaller amount of Outro and extra ATK% buffs (which Mortefi easily accesses via the Static Mist pistol and his S6). Additionally, her higher rotation time ultimately makes her only worth slotting on Augusta's team if your Mortefi is already taken by another character or if you like Yinlin (as technically it's Yinlin's new best team, just not the other way around).

Similarly to Xiangli Yao, Yinlin's good personal off-field damage and her extremely important 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplify on Outro buffs Calcharo a major amount, while also being able to trade those buffs off for consistency by abusing each other's many Swap Cancel windows, making the pair natural.

Yinlin is actually the character Youhu buffs the most, due to Yinlin having the highest personal damage of any Coordinated Attack DPS in the game and her ability to amplify Coordinated Attack DMG by 100% on Outro. As a result, the pairing is natural, while it doesn't compare to 5 star supports.

One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.

Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
